The petitioners have challenged the prosecution initiated by the respondent No.1 in Crime No.214/2019 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 418, 420, 424 read with Section 34 of IPC pending trial before the XI Additional chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru City.

sentences.text:
2. The respondent No.2 herein lodged a complaint before the respondent No.1 on 26.04.2019 stating therein that he, petitioner No.1 and three others were the Directors of M/s. Dreamquest Infotech Private Limited (henceforth referred to as 'Dreamquest') whose primary business was providing I.T.
infrastructure and services.
He claimed that they were also NC: 2023:KHC:29500 into the business of breeding live stock and were holding shares in the company.
He claimed that the company was run by the Directors out of their own investment and later out of profits earned from Dreamquest.

He alleged that he and the accused No.1 and other Directors floated another company called Fiza Plantations Private Limited (henceforth referred to as 'Fiza Plantations') in the year 2001 and each of them were holding 25% of stake in the company.
He claimed that out of the profits earned from Dreamquest over a period of three years, 40 acres of coffee plantation in Koraput, Orissa was purchased which was later sold on 26.02.2007.
The sale proceeds were received in the name of Fiza Plantation, which was invested for purchase of 16-7 acres in Vattadahosalli village, Nagaragere Hobli, Gowribidanur Taluk.

He claimed that the Directors of the Fiza Plantation were not agriculturists and therefore, out of mutual understanding, the accused No.1 and his father (accused No.2) agreed that the property may be purchased in the name of accused No.2.
Consequently, the sale deed was executed on 19.09.2007 in respect of 16 - 7 acres in the name of accused No.2.

It was agreed that the property would be transferred to the individual names of the Directors after NC:
2023:KHC:29500 obtaining permission for purchase of agricultural land.
He alleged that the sale proceeds received by Fiza Plantation from the sale of the property in Koraput, Orissa was utilized for purchase of the land in Vattadahosalli village.
He alleged that after purchase of the land, the profits from Dreamquest was diverted for further development of the property and for payment of salary for the labourers.

Likewise, another property situate at Bengaluru city was purchased by Masood Ahmed vs State Of Karnataka on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35347766/
2 Dreamquest which later on became the office premises of Dreamquest.

sentences.text:
He alleged that the accused No.1 went on postponing the transfer of his share at Vattadahosalli village and in the year 2010,
when he insisted for executing proper documents, accused No.1 refused to transfer the property and started claiming that it was his individual property.
He alleged that the accused No.1 restrained him from entering into the property with an intention to cause wrongful loss and to cheat him.
Thereafter, accused No.1 started harassing him which compelled him to resign from the company.
He also alleged that the accused No.1 was promising to transfer his share of agricultural land and settle the account.
However, accused No.1 after obtaining a resignation refused to transfer the agricultural land and NC: 2023:KHC:29500 undervalued his share at 50% of the value settled to the other Directors.
He therefore, claimed that the accused had defrauded him by undervaluing the office premises of Dreamquest and transferring it to the name of accused No.2 in terms of sale deed dated 20.07.2010.
He also alleged that the accused No.2 further undervalued the property to Rs.1,60,00,000/- and sold it to third party and swindled the entire sale proceeds along with accused No.1.

He alleged that he came to know of the fraud only when he tried to initiate legal process at which point, the accused No.1 called him back and offered 40% stake in the company and also promised to transfer the property and make good the financial loss suffered by him.
He alleged that after being reinstated as Director of Dreamquest, he realized that it was another trap for him and slowly accused No.1 started refusing to share any profit.

Thus, he alleged that the accused had misappropriated the funds of Dreamquest by transferring the property at Vattadahosahalli village to the name of accused No.2 and the property at Bengaluru city which was valued at a sum of Rs.3,50,00,000/-.
He claimed that 40% of the amount cheated by the accused No.1 was valued at Rs.2,60,00,000/-.
Therefore, he prayed NC: 2023:KHC:29500 that suitable action be initiated against the accused.

Based on this, Crime No.214/2019 was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 418, 420, 424 read with Section 34 of IPC.
3.
The accused Nos.1 and 2 have therefore, challenged the prosecution initiated against them in this petition.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the respondent No.2 having resigned from the company on his own, cannot contend that the amount settled to him did not correspond to his share in the value of the company.
He submitted that the respondent No.2 had gone out of the company on his own and after exiting from the company, he has lodged false complaint against the accused.
He further claimed that though the property was purchased in the name of the accused No.2 in the year 2010, the respondent No.2 did not take any action till the year 2019.

At any rate, he contends that this was essentially a civil dispute between the parties and if the respondent No.2 was aggrieved by any action in the working of the company, it is open for him to take such steps as are provided in law.
Though the respondent No.2 is represented by a counsel, she has remained absent in the forenoon session as well as in the afternoon session.
Therefore, this Court did not have the benefit of her submission.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The fact that an agricultural property was purchased from out of the funds of Dreamquest in the name of accused No.2 to avoid a prohibition in law i.e. Section 80 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, makes it clear that the respondent No.2 had conceded that the property would remain in the name of the accused No.2.

If the respondent No.2 had settled the dispute with the accused No.1 and had exited the company by submitting his resignation in the year 2010, he cannot now turn around and claim that his resignation was obtained fraudulently.
He also cannot claim that he was defrauded and that the value of the shares at the time of his exiting was undervalued.

Certainly,
respondent No.2 could not have accused the petitioners of committing an offences under Sections 406, 418, 420, 424 read with Section 34 of IPC.
A perusal of the entire complaint does not indicate as to how the accused had committed the offences under Sections 406, 418, 420, 424 read with Section 34 of IPC.
In that view of the NC: 2023:KHC:29500 matter, the prosecution of the petitioners is wholly unwarranted and is not justified.

If the respondent No.2 is aggrieved by any action of Dreamquest or Fiza Plantations, it is for him to approach the Tribunal under Section 213 of Companies Act, 2013 or the Registrar of Companies under Section 212 of the Companies Act, 2013 for suitable action.
7. Consequently, this petition is allowed.

The impugned prosecution of the petitioners in Crime No.214/2019 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 418, 420, 424 read with Section 34 of IPC pending trial before the XI Additional chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru City, is quashed.
